extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal education funds (K-12 and postsecondary institutions), Title IX Coordinators, institutional legal/compliance staff, and grievance procedure administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance and required standards for recipient grievance procedures under Title IX, including who may file complaints, Title IX Coordinator authority, protections against bias, investigative and evidentiary standards, supportive measures, appeals, and related procedural safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator initiation authority (§106.44(f)(1)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: In the absence of a complaint (or after withdrawal/termination of informal resolution), the Title IX Coordinator may initiate a complaint only after determining that the alleged conduct "presents an imminent and serious threat to the health or safety of a complainant or other person, or that conduct as alleged prevents the recipient from ensuring equal access based on sex to its education program or activity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In making this fact-specific determination the Title IX Coordinator must consider at minimum the factors listed in §106.44(f)(1)(v)(A)(1)-(8): the complainant's request not to proceed; complainant's reasonable safety concerns; risk of additional acts of sex discrimination if procedures not initiated; severity of alleged sex discrimination (including potential removal of respondent or other sanctions); age and relationship of the parties (including whether respondent is an employee); scope (pattern, ongoing discrimination, multiple individuals); availability of evidence; and whether the recipient could end or prevent recurrence without initiating grievance procedures. This decision-making requirement makes initiation extremely unlikely to be based on misunderstanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a complaint (§106.45(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: For complaints alleging sex-based harassment, only a complainant (the person alleged to have been subjected), a parent/guardian/authorized legal representative, or the Title IX Coordinator may file. For sex discrimination that is not sex-based harassment, complaints may be filed by those persons and also by any student or employee or any person participating or attempting to participate in the recipient's education program or activity at the time of the alleged conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation clarifies that this does not mean anyone who claims knowledge can force an investigation; there are clear category limits depending on whether the allegation is of sex-based harassment. Recipients may permissively dismiss complaints under §106.45(d)(1)(i)-(iv), including where alleged conduct, even if proven, would not constitute sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures—scope and appropriateness (§106.44(g), §106.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer supportive measures “as appropriate” to restore or preserve a party's access to the recipient's education program or activity, including measures designed to protect safety and the educational environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient's obligations toward third parties (non-students/employees) may be limited by lack of relationship; when not appropriate or necessary to restore access, the recipient need not offer supportive measures. Supportive measures and their timing are discussed in connection with §106.44(f)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat complainants and respondents equitably (§106.45(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's grievance procedures must treat complainants and respondents equitably throughout the grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is broader than providing supportive measures or following grievance procedures before imposing sanctions; equitability applies throughout. It applies regardless of the sex of the parties and is consistent with nondiscrimination requirements in §106.31(a) and (b)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable treatment may differ from equal treatment (explanation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Equitable treatment does not necessarily mean strictly equal treatment; it means fundamental fairness and recognizing that the interests of complainant and respondent may differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include providing remedies to a complainant if discrimination is found, using grievance procedures before imposing discipline on a respondent, and offering supportive measures at different times. The regulations declined to define 'equitably' in narrow terms, explaining existing provisions collectively require procedures free of favoritism or bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartial investigation requirement (§106.45(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide for an adequate, reliable, and impartial investigation of complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An impartial investigation is necessary for equitable adjudication; related provisions require investigators to be trained to serve impartially and avoid prejudgment, conflicts of interest, and bias (see §106.8(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conflicts of interest or bias for designated officials (§106.45(b)(2), §106.44(k)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons designated as Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decisionmakers, and informal resolution facilitators must not have a conflict of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally or an individual complainant or respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibition applies to all decisionmakers, including those deciding appeals of dismissals. The Department declined to identify specific job roles that would presumptively create a conflict, leaving recipients discretion. Recipients must take steps (including training and disclosure where appropriate) to prevent bias; appeals may be based on decisionmaker conflict of interest or bias where it would change the outcome (§106.46(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of respondent not responsible (§106.45(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must include a presumption that the respondent is not responsible for the alleged sex discrimination until a determination is made at the conclusion of the grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This presumption is a required element promoting fairness in the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective evaluation of evidence and prohibited credibility bases (§106.45(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must require an objective evaluation of all evidence that is relevant and not otherwise impermissible, and credibility determinations must not be based on a person's status as a complainant, respondent, or witness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcomes must not be based on stereotyping; recipients must remove barriers to reporting for communities that have historically faced discrimination. The regulation aims to prevent stereotyped or biased outcomes against complainants of color, LGBTQI+ complainants, and complainants with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trauma-informed approach is discretionary but must comply with regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may use a trauma-informed approach (considering signs/symptoms of trauma and avoiding re-traumatization) if it complies with the final regulations, including fairness and impartiality requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to require or prohibit specific terminology (e.g., 'survivor' vs. 'complainant')—recipients may use terms as they choose so long as procedures meet requirements (no bias, objective evaluation). Concerns that trauma-informed approaches create bias were addressed by tying such approaches to existing anti-bias provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy protections during grievance procedures (§106.45(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must take reasonable steps to protect the privacy of the parties and witnesses during the grievance procedures, subject to certain exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Privacy protections are balanced against other obligations and exceptions; the provision helps prevent unnecessary disclosure of sensitive information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional grievance provisions must apply equally to parties (§106.45(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient adopts additional provisions as part of its grievance procedures beyond those required by the regulations, those additional provisions must apply equally to the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement was broadened from the 2020 amendments to apply to grievance procedures for all forms of sex discrimination, not only sex-based harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must follow grievance procedures before imposing discipline (§106.45(h)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must comply with the grievance procedure requirements in §106.45, and if applicable §106.46, before imposing any disciplinary sanctions against a respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects due process and ensures discipline follows the prescribed procedural safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on disciplining for statements or consensual conduct (§106.45(h)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are precluded from disciplining a party, witness, or others participating in the grievance procedures for making a false statement or for engaging in consensual sexual conduct based solely on the recipient's determination whether sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision protects participants from unfair sanctions that could chill reporting or participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissive dismissal rules (§106.45(d)(1)(i)-(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: The permissive dismissal rules apply to all complaints; a recipient can dismiss a complaint on any listed bases (including where alleged conduct, even if proven, would not constitute sex discrimination under Title IX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissive dismissals provide a check against frivolous or inapplicable claims; dismissed complaints may be subject to appeal under the recipient's appeal procedures where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals—minimum and postsecondary-specific bases (§106.45(i), §106.46(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer parties an appeal that, at minimum, is the same as they offer in other comparable proceedings. For postsecondary institutions, appeals must be available on bases that would change material aspects of the matter, including procedural irregularity or decisionmaker conflict of interest or bias that would change the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals serve as a procedural safeguard; conflicts of interest or bias that would change outcome are explicit grounds for appeal in postsecondary settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirements include anti-bias and neutrality (§106.8(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are required to train investigators (and other designated persons) on how to serve impartially, including by avoiding prejudgment of the facts at issue, conflicts of interest, and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department regarded training as a key safeguard against bias and declined to add more categorical conflict-of-interest restrictions, relying instead on training, procedural checks, appeals, and OCR enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of 'sex discrimination' in definition (reference to §106.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations clarify that sex discrimination includes, but is not limited to, discrimination based on sex stereotypes, sex characteristics, pregnancy or related conditions, sexual orientation, and gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This broad understanding supports allowing complaints by non-aggrieved persons in some cases and informs the scope of what grievance procedures must address.
